description.narrative: Ghana has a legal and policy framework that supports freedom of expression and the safety of journalists. However, despite the relatively conducive environment in which the media operate, freedom of expression is still infringed upon by state and non-state actors, including members of security agencies. Over the years, UNESCO has worked to improve freedom of expression and the safety of journalists by training members of the judiciary and security agencies, and by establishing a national monitoring mechanism for journalists’ safety. Together with partners, UNESCO will implement a range of activities along the Plan's "three Ps" (prevention, protection and prosecution) through: - awareness-raising - monitoring and reporting - capacity building and partnership building - supporting mechanisms for the safety of journalists - addressing the specific risks faced by women journalists, compounded by technology-facilitated gender-based violence in an era of generative AI These activities will directly contribute to Outcome 5.1, on freedom of expression and the safety of journalists.
